problems.name: Flat tire
problems.summary: The tire has lost most of its air, usually from a nail, a pothole or a slow leak that finally gave out.
tools: The jack that came with the car
Wheel chock or a heavy stone
steps: Park on firm, level ground well away from traffic, with the car in Park and the parking brake on.
Loosen each lug nut half a turn while the wheel is still on the ground.
Set the jack at the lift point marked in the owner's manual and raise the car until the tire is clear of the ground.
Remove the nuts, swap the wheel and tighten the nuts by hand in a star pattern.
Lower the car, then tighten the nuts fully in a star pattern.
Keep to 50 mph (80 km/h) or less on a compact spare and have the tire repaired soon.
problems.videoQuery: how to change a flat tire
problems.stopIf: There is no usable spare, the rim is bent, or the ground is soft or sloped. Call for a tow or a mobile tire service.

problems.name: Tire pressure warning light
problems.summary: One or more tires is below the recommended pressure. A cold night or a slow leak is the usual cause.
tools: The pressure sticker inside the driver's door frame
steps: Read the cold pressure on the sticker inside the driver's door frame.
Remove each valve cap and measure every tire.
Inflate each low tire to the pressure on the sticker.
Drive for 15 minutes, then check the pressures again.
If one tire keeps losing air, look for a nail or a damaged valve.
problems.videoQuery: tire pressure warning light inflate reset
problems.stopIf: The tire drops again within an hour. Have it patched at a tire shop.

problems.name: Leaking valve stem
problems.summary: Air is escaping at the valve, usually through a loose or worn valve core.
steps: Spray soapy water on the valve. Bubbles show where the air is escaping.
Tighten the valve core clockwise with the tool.
If it still leaks, fit a new valve core.
Inflate to the pressure on the door sticker and test again with soapy water.
Refit the valve cap.
problems.videoQuery: replace leaking tire valve core
problems.stopIf: The rubber stem is cracked or split. A tire shop has to replace it.

problems.name: Sidewall bulge or blowout
problems.summary: A bulge, or a shredded tire, means the tire's structure has failed. It can burst without warning.
tools: Full-size spare, if you carry one
steps: Ease off the accelerator and hold the wheel straight. Avoid hard braking after a blowout.
Move fully onto the shoulder and turn on your hazard lights.
Do not drive on a bulged tire, even slowly.
Fit the spare only if you are well clear of traffic.
Otherwise call for a tow or a mobile tire service.
problems.videoQuery: tire blowout what to do
problems.stopIf: Always. A bulge or exposed cords cannot be repaired.

problems.name: Loose or missing lug nuts
problems.summary: A click, clunk or wobble from one wheel can mean loose lug nuts, often after recent tire work.
tools: A spare nut, or one borrowed from the other wheels
steps: Stop and check every wheel by hand.
Tighten each nut in a star pattern.
If a nut is missing, take one nut from each of the other wheels so that no wheel is short by more than one.
Check the nuts again after 25 miles (40 km).
Have a shop tighten them to the specified torque.
problems.videoQuery: tighten lug nuts star pattern
problems.stopIf: A stud is bent, broken or stripped. Do not drive; call for a tow.

problems.name: Shaking at speed
problems.summary: A shudder through the steering wheel at 55 to 70 mph (90 to 110 km/h) usually means an unbalanced wheel or a rim bent by a pothole.
steps: Check the pressure in all four tires.
Look for bulges, missing balance weights or a bent rim.
Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Stay below the speed at which it shakes.
Have the wheels balanced at a tire shop.
problems.videoQuery: car shakes at highway speed
problems.stopIf: The shaking gets worse, or you hear grinding. Pull over and call for help.

problems.name: Dead battery
problems.summary: Fast clicking, or no crank at all, together with dim dash lights points to a flat battery.
tools: Portable jump starter, or jumper cables and a second car
steps: Switch off the lights and every accessory.
With a jump pack, clamp red to the positive (+) post of the flat battery and black to bare, unpainted metal on the engine, away from the battery.
With cables, add the second car: red to both positive posts, black to the good battery's negative post, then black to bare metal on the flat car. Start the helper car first.
Switch on the jump pack, or let the helper car run for a few minutes, then start your car.
Drive for at least 30 minutes to recharge.
problems.videoQuery: how to jump start a car
problems.stopIf: The battery is swollen or leaking, or the car dies again soon after. Many parts stores test batteries for free.

problems.name: Battery light while driving
problems.summary: A battery light, dimming headlights or a whine means the alternator has stopped charging. The car runs on the battery until it is empty.
tools: Phone charger, unplugged to save power
Jump starter, in case the car stalls
steps: Switch off the air conditioning, radio, seat heaters and chargers.
Keep the headlights on only if it is dark.
Drive straight to the nearest parts store or garage.
Do not switch the engine off before you arrive.
Ask for a charging system test.
problems.videoQuery: alternator failing symptoms battery light
problems.stopIf: The gauges flicker or the steering gets heavy. Pull over safely now.

problems.name: One click, then nothing
problems.summary: A single loud click with bright dash lights means the battery is fine but the starter motor is not turning.
steps: Check that the dash lights stay bright when you turn the key.
Try again with the gear selector in Neutral instead of Park. Some cars start in either.
If the dash lights dim a lot when you turn the key, treat it as a flat battery instead.
If it still will not turn, call for a tow.
problems.videoQuery: car clicks once but won't start
problems.stopIf: You smell burning from under the car. Stop trying and call for help.

problems.name: Out of fuel
problems.summary: The engine cranks but will not fire, and the fuel gauge reads empty or close to it.
tools: Approved fuel can holding 1 to 2 gallons (4 to 8 liters), or a fuel delivery service
steps: Coast fully onto the shoulder and turn on your hazard lights.
Ask for fuel delivery through your insurer or roadside plan. Do not walk along a highway.
Add at least 1 to 2 gallons (4 to 8 liters).
Crank in bursts of no more than five seconds until fuel reaches the engine.
Fill the tank at the next station.
problems.videoQuery: ran out of gas what to do
problems.stopIf: The gauge shows fuel but the car still will not start. It may be the fuel pump; have it towed.

problems.name: Wrong fuel in the tank
problems.summary: Diesel in a gasoline car, or gasoline in a diesel car, can badly damage the fuel system once the engine runs.
steps: Do not start the engine. If you have only just filled up, do not switch the ignition on either.
If you are already driving, pull over safely and switch off at once.
Move the car away from the pump only with help and only if it is safe.
Call for a tow to a garage that can drain the tank.
problems.videoQuery: wrong fuel in car what to do
problems.stopIf: Always. Running the engine can ruin the fuel pump and injectors.

problems.name: Key fob dead or key not detected
problems.summary: The buttons do nothing, or the dash says that no key is detected.
tools: New coin battery (most fobs use a CR2032 or CR2025)
Small flat screwdriver or a coin
steps: On a push-button car, hold the fob against the start button and press the brake to start.
Use the hidden metal key inside the fob to open the door.
Pry the fob open at its seam.
Fit the new battery with the + side facing the same way as the old one.
Close the fob and test lock, unlock and start.
problems.videoQuery: key fob battery replacement
problems.stopIf: It still fails with a new battery. A dealer may need to reprogram the key.

problems.name: Check engine light, steady
problems.summary: A steady light means the engine computer has logged a fault that is not urgent. A loose fuel cap is a common cause.
tools: Most parts stores read codes for free
steps: Tighten the fuel cap until it clicks.
Check that the car drives normally, with no shaking and no loss of power.
Carry on gently to your destination.
Have the code read at a parts store or a garage.
The light can clear itself after a few drives if the fault was minor.
problems.videoQuery: check engine light steady what to do
problems.stopIf: The light starts flashing, or the car loses power. Pull over.

problems.name: Check engine light, flashing
problems.summary: A flashing light signals a serious misfire. Unburned fuel can overheat and destroy the catalytic converter.
steps: Ease off the accelerator and lighten the load on the engine.
Pull off at the first safe place.
Switch the engine off.
Call for a tow instead of driving on.
problems.videoQuery: flashing check engine light misfire
problems.stopIf: Always. Damage is happening while the light flashes.

problems.name: Oil pressure light
problems.summary: A red oil can light means low oil pressure, most often because the oil level is low.
tools: 1 to 2 quarts (1 to 2 liters) of oil of the grade printed on the oil filler cap
steps: Switch the engine off right away.
Wait five minutes on level ground.
Pull the dipstick, wipe it, push it back in fully and read the level.
Add oil half a quart (half a liter) at a time, up to the full mark.
Restart. The light should go out within seconds.
problems.videoQuery: how to check and add engine oil
problems.stopIf: The light stays on with the oil full, or you hear knocking. Do not drive; call for a tow.

problems.name: Hybrid or electric system warning
problems.summary: A message such as check hybrid system, or a high voltage warning, means the electric drive has a fault. These systems carry dangerous voltage.
steps: Pull over safely and put the car in Park.
Switch the car fully off for two minutes, then restart once.
If the warning comes back, do not drive.
Never touch the orange cables.
Call for a tow to a dealer that services hybrid or electric cars.
problems.videoQuery: check hybrid system warning what to do
problems.stopIf: You see smoke or smell burning from a hybrid or electric car. Get out and move well away from it.

problems.name: Engine overheating
problems.summary: The temperature gauge is in the red, or steam is rising from the hood. Low coolant, a failed fan or a stuck thermostat is the usual cause.
tools: Premixed 50/50 coolant of the type in your manual
1 gallon (4 liters) of water as an emergency backup
steps: Turn the heater to full hot to draw heat away from the engine.
Pull over and switch the engine off.
Wait at least 30 minutes. Never open a hot radiator cap.
Top up the coolant reservoir to the MAX mark.
Restart and watch the gauge and the cooling fans.
problems.videoQuery: engine overheating what to do roadside
problems.stopIf: The gauge climbs again within minutes, or coolant pours out. Call for a tow.

problems.name: Coolant leak
problems.summary: A sweet, syrupy smell, or a green, orange or pink puddle under the front of the car.
tools: Radiator stop-leak, as a temporary fix
steps: Let the engine cool completely.
Look for wet spots on the hoses and clamps.
Tighten any loose hose clamp.
For a small leak, add stop-leak as the bottle directs.
Refill the coolant and check the level at every stop.
problems.videoQuery: find and fix coolant leak radiator hose
problems.stopIf: A hose has split or the radiator is cracked. A temporary fix will not last.

problems.name: Broken drive belt
problems.summary: A loud squeal or slap, then a battery light, heavy steering and a rising temperature. One belt drives the alternator, the water pump and, on many cars, power steering.
steps: Pull over before the engine overheats.
Once the engine is cool, open the hood and look for a missing or shredded belt.
Do not drive any further than a short distance to a safe spot.
Call for a tow. A garage can often fit a new belt the same day.
problems.videoQuery: serpentine belt broke symptoms
problems.stopIf: Always. Without the belt the engine overheats within minutes.

problems.name: Smoke from the exhaust or a burning smell
problems.summary: Blue smoke means burning oil, white smoke with a sweet smell means coolant, and black smoke means too much fuel.
steps: Note the color of the smoke and the smell.
Once the engine is cool, check the oil and coolant levels.
Look for oil dripping onto the exhaust.
Top up whichever is low.
Drive gently to a garage and tell them the color of the smoke.
problems.videoQuery: exhaust smoke color meaning
problems.stopIf: Thick white smoke comes with overheating, or smoke comes from under the hood. Stop and call for a tow.

problems.name: Sudden loss of power
problems.summary: The car will not go above about 25 mph (40 km/h), or will not shift. The computer is limiting power to protect the engine or transmission.
steps: Switch on your hazard lights and move to the edge of the road.
Leave at the next safe place and switch the car off.
Wait five minutes and restart.
Check the oil and coolant levels.
Drive slowly to a garage for a code scan.
problems.videoQuery: car limp mode what to do
problems.stopIf: It comes back at once, or the check engine light flashes. Call for a tow.

problems.name: Transmission slipping
problems.summary: The engine revs but the car does not speed up, or shifts are late and harsh.
tools: Transmission fluid of the exact type in your manual
steps: Pull over and let the car cool for 20 minutes.
Check the fluid if your car has a transmission dipstick. Many newer cars do not.
Top up with the exact fluid type.
Drive gently and avoid hard acceleration.
Have a transmission shop check it.
problems.videoQuery: transmission slipping symptoms
problems.stopIf: The car will not move in Drive or Reverse. Call for a tow.

problems.name: Squealing or grinding brakes
problems.summary: A high squeal is the wear indicator on worn pads. Grinding is metal on metal and damages the discs.
steps: Leave extra space to the car ahead.
Brake earlier and more gently.
Look through the wheel spokes to see how much pad is left.
If it is grinding, see a garage the same day.
problems.videoQuery: brake noise squeal versus grinding
problems.stopIf: The pedal feels soft, or the car pulls hard when you brake. Stop and call for a tow.

problems.name: Soft or sinking brake pedal
problems.summary: A pedal that sinks toward the floor means a fluid leak or air in the lines. Stopping power is reduced.
steps: Pump the pedal and shift down to slow the car.
Use the parking brake gently if you need it.
Leave the road at the first safe place.
Look for fluid near the wheels.
Do not drive. Call for a tow.
problems.videoQuery: spongy brake pedal causes
problems.stopIf: Always. Brakes cannot be patched well enough to limp home.

problems.name: Car pulls to one side
problems.summary: Uneven tire pressure is the usual cause. If it pulls only when you brake, a brake caliper may be sticking.
steps: Check all four pressures and make them match.
Look for a soft or damaged tire.
After driving, hold your hand near each wheel. A very hot one points to a sticking brake.
Ask for an alignment check at a tire shop.
problems.videoQuery: car pulls to one side causes
problems.stopIf: A wheel smokes or smells of burning. Pull over and let it cool.

problems.name: Heavy or whining steering
problems.summary: Low power steering fluid or a failing pump makes the wheel heavy, often with a whine when turning.
tools: Power steering fluid of the type in your manual
steps: Check whether your car has a fluid reservoir. Electric systems do not.
Top up to the marked line.
Look under the front of the car for leaks.
Drive slowly. The steering still works, it just needs more effort.
problems.videoQuery: power steering heavy whining fluid
problems.stopIf: The steering suddenly locks or becomes very heavy at speed. Pull over.

problems.name: Blown fuse: charger or radio dead
problems.summary: One circuit, such as the charging socket or the radio, stopped suddenly. A fuse has probably blown.
tools: Fuse puller, often clipped inside the fuse box lid
Fuse diagram from the owner's manual
steps: Find the fuse box under the dash or under the hood.
Match the dead circuit on the diagram.
Pull the fuse. A broken metal strip means it has blown.
Fit a new fuse with the same amp rating.
Test the circuit.
problems.videoQuery: how to replace a blown car fuse
problems.stopIf: The new fuse blows at once. There is a short circuit; see a mechanic.

problems.name: Headlight or brake light out
problems.summary: A bulb warning on the dash, or someone points it out. A dead brake light is a common reason to be stopped by the police.
tools: Replacement bulb of the right type
steps: Ask the parts store for the exact bulb number for your car.
Open the hood, or the trunk liner behind the light.
Twist out the bulb holder.
Fit the new bulb without touching the glass.
Test it before you close everything up.
problems.videoQuery: replace headlight bulb
problems.stopIf: It is an LED or sealed unit, which cannot be swapped at the roadside. Go to a garage.

problems.name: Wipers stopped working
problems.summary: Usually a blown fuse or a loose wiper arm nut. In rain this is a safety problem.
steps: Pull over and wait until the rain eases.
Check the wiper fuse.
See whether the motor runs but the arm does not move. That points to a loose nut.
Apply rain repellent to the glass.
Drive slowly and leave extra distance.
problems.videoQuery: windshield wipers stopped working fix
problems.stopIf: Heavy rain and no wipers. Stay parked until you can see clearly.

problems.name: Air conditioning blows warm
problems.summary: Usually low refrigerant, a blown air conditioning fuse or a compressor clutch that will not engage.
tools: AC recharge kit with a gauge (check your manual for the refrigerant type)
steps: Start the engine and set the air conditioning to maximum.
Check that the compressor clutch is turning.
Connect the gauge to the low-pressure port only.
Add refrigerant in short bursts, watching the gauge.
Stop in the green zone. Do not overfill.
problems.videoQuery: car ac blowing warm air recharge
problems.stopIf: The compressor will not engage, or the charge leaks out fast. It needs a shop.

problems.name: No heat
problems.summary: Cold air from the heater usually means low coolant or a stuck thermostat. In winter this is a safety matter.
steps: Check that the temperature gauge reaches its normal position.
Once the engine is cool, top up the coolant.
Use the defroster to keep the windshield clear.
Dress warmly and keep a blanket within reach.
Have the cooling system checked soon.
problems.videoQuery: car heater blowing cold air
problems.stopIf: The gauge stays low and the windows ice over inside. Stop somewhere warm.

problems.name: Windshield will not clear
problems.summary: Fog stays on the glass, often because recirculation is on or the cabin filter is clogged.
tools: Cabin air filter, if airflow is weak
steps: Turn recirculation off so the car draws in fresh air.
Turn on the air conditioning with the defroster. It dries the air.
Set the temperature to warm and the fan to high.
Wipe the glass with the microfiber cloth.
Replace the cabin filter if the airflow is weak.
problems.videoQuery: how to defog windshield fast
problems.stopIf: A sweet smell with a greasy film on the glass. The heater core may be leaking; see a mechanic.

problems.name: Musty smell or weak airflow
problems.summary: A musty smell and weak airflow mean the cabin air filter is clogged.
tools: Cabin air filter for your exact vehicle
steps: Empty the glove box.
Release the stops so the glove box swings down.
Slide out the filter door and the old filter.
Fit the new filter with its airflow arrow matching the one on the housing.
Refit everything and run the fan on high.
problems.videoQuery: cabin air filter replacement
problems.stopIf: The smell stays after a new filter. The evaporator may need a professional clean.

problems.name: Stuck in snow or mud
problems.summary: The wheels spin and the car does not move. Common on snowy shoulders and soft verges.
tools: Cat litter, sand or floor mats for grip
steps: Switch off traction control with the button on the dash.
Clear snow or mud from around the driven wheels.
Put litter, sand or a floor mat in front of the tires.
Accelerate gently and rock between Drive and Reverse.
If you wait with the engine running, keep the exhaust pipe clear and open a window slightly.
problems.videoQuery: how to get a car unstuck from snow
problems.stopIf: The car is near a ditch, or you are blocking traffic. Call for a tow.

problems.name: Keys locked in the car
problems.summary: The keys are inside and the doors are locked.
tools: Your car brand's phone app, if it can unlock remotely
steps: Check every door and the trunk release.
Try your car brand's phone app to unlock.
Call roadside assistance. Lockouts are often covered.
If a child or a pet is inside, or it is hot, call your local emergency number right away.
problems.videoQuery: locked keys in car what to do
problems.stopIf: Do not use a wire hanger on a modern car. It can damage airbag wiring and door electronics.

problems.name: Hit an animal
problems.summary: Animal strikes are common at dawn and dusk on rural roads.
steps: Pull over with your hazard lights on and keep away from the animal.
Call the police if the animal is blocking the road or the damage is serious.
Check for leaks, broken lights and a damaged radiator.
Take photos for your insurer.
Drive on only if the lights work and nothing is leaking.
problems.videoQuery: what to do after hitting a deer
problems.stopIf: Fluid is leaking, a headlight is out at night, or the hood will not latch. Call for a tow.

problems.name: Minor accident, no injuries
problems.summary: A fender bender where everyone is unhurt and the cars can still move.
tools: Driver's license, registration and insurance details
steps: Check that everyone is unhurt. Call your local emergency number if anyone is not.
Move the cars out of the traffic lanes if they can be driven.
Swap names, phone numbers, insurance details and plate numbers.
Photograph both cars, the scene and the other driver's documents.
Call your insurer from the scene.
problems.videoQuery: what to do after a minor car accident
problems.stopIf: Anyone is hurt, an airbag went off, or fluid is leaking. Call your local emergency number.
